anna (eng-ml): Heads-up: after flipping the new 'slew' kernel selector + AWQ group_size=32 default, we see a regression on our INT8 weight-only path in staging. p95 latency up ~18% and tokens/sec down ~22% for short chats. :eyes:

mike (eng-runtime): ugh. which commit/flags? are we seeing more unpack/pack overhead or kernel scatter?

anna (eng-ml): rolled from commit abc123 -> def456 (kernel-selector: slew heuristics). Flags: --group-size 32 --pack-align 64 --kvcache-prefetch=true. Benchmark run: bench-chat --model=llama-awq-int8 --seq=64 --batch=8 --workers=8

anna (eng-ml): quick numbers (median of 10 runs):
```
old (kernel=legacy): p50 38ms p95 92ms tokens/s 420
new (kernel=slew):   p50 44ms p95 109ms tokens/s 328
```

kai (eng-ml): that's a nasty drop. any perf profile (nvprof/trace) showing time split? kernel compute vs packing?

anna (eng-ml): grabbed hot traces and flamegraph from runtime profiler. top of stack shows much more time in pack_serial_copy + memcpy paths. Also KV cache slice lookups up slightly. attaching snippet:
```
# sampled stack counts
pack_serial_copy (memcpy) 38%\nmatmul_awq_slew_kernel 27%\nkv_cache_lookup 9%\nother 26%\n```

sophia (eng-platform): could be alignment/padding effect from pack-align 64. slewing might change group placement so we end up with more partial slabs and memcpy. Did we change the packer strategy?

anna (eng-ml): yes we adjusted packer to prefer packing by contiguous group count to favor fewer kernel launches. With slew selector, kernels expect group-aligned buffers and we added pad to 64 bytes to avoid unaligned loads. That added extra mem copies for small sequences.

mike (eng-runtime): hypothesis: slew picks a kernel variant that is faster for large groups but for our typical short-chat seq=64 the packing overhead kills it. We should add a policy: for seq <= 128 and batch <= 8 prefer legacy kernel or use group_size=16 fallback. Can we reproduce perf cliff with a micro-bench?

anna (eng-ml): reproduced with micro-bench. Script: `./bench_pack --kernel-slew --group-size 32 --seq 64 --iters 100` shows steady overhead in pack_serial_copy. When I forced group_size=16 the tokens/s returned to ~410.

kai (eng-ml): interesting — also check cache residency: with different pack alignment we might be evicting more KV pages causing extra kv_cache_lookup. Any memory traffic numbers?

anna (eng-ml): yes: mem BW up ~12%, LLC miss rate +6%. So both memcpy overhead + cache pressure. I tried enabling `prefetch=false` and that shaved ~3% but not enough.

mike (eng-runtime): can we adjust kernel selection cost model to include pack-overhead estimate? currently it only models compute cycles. Add a simple heuristic: estimated_pack_cost = groups * group_size * C_mem + padding_penalty. If estimated_pack_cost > threshold, demote slew variant.

sophia (eng-platform): sounds good. Also short-term revert: set default group_size to 16 for hosted/staging until we land a calibrated selector. Keep dedicated customers on their pinned configs.

anna (eng-ml): implementing a fast binary: compare kernels on micro-bench for the typical seq/batch distribution and write a telemetry event with chosen variant + pack_cost. That will let Optimize suggest group_size knobs automatically.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for rollback-config (user: sophia) to staging at 2026-03-18T15:42:00Z :truck: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike (eng-runtime): follow-up tasks:
- add pack_cost estimate to kernel selector (PR by mike)
- telemetry event for chosen variant + measured pack_time (PR by anna)
- add short-chat rule in policy: seq<=128 & batch<=8 -> prefer legacy/group<=16 (config change by sophia)

kai (eng-ml): also add unit test that simulates small sequence batches and ensures selector prefers low-pack-overhead kernel.

anna (eng-ml): I'll open the bench traces/artefacts in the perf board and paste links, plus a small diff for packer to try eager coalescing which may reduce memcpy count.

sophia (eng-platform): rolling rollback done, staging metrics back to baseline. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-runtime): great. once PRs land we'll rerun the calibration sweep and gate slew variant with a measured win in our seq/batch distribution.

anna (eng-ml): logs and flamegraphs: https://internal.redwood/trace/1765432100-pprof (private link)

kai (eng-ml): nice investigation, good to quantify pack overhead. leaving a note to inspect AWQ quant calibration too — different quant scales can change kernel packing density and affect this in subtle ways.

anna (eng-ml): noted. next step: add quant-scale-aware packer heuristic to avoid worst-case alignment combos.

mike (eng-runtime): tagging this as action item in the runtime board (#RT-1127).
